content_of_post_to_answer: Why does the ticking sound from a Pomodoro timer help you concentrate better?
answer: The ticking sound may work less because it "helps you focus" and more because it removes the uncertainty that usually drains attention. A normal timer creates pressure; a steady tick creates a predictable rhythm, giving the brain a stable external cue to organize around. It is similar to how musicians use a metronome: the goal is not the sound itself, but reducing the mental effort of deciding when to move forward. The interesting part is that the timer is not adding discipline—it is outsourcing part of the discipline to the environment.
